Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. ## PR Description

### What changed
- `preCliDevelopmentSetup` now asserts the dev-leg transition itself: clears stale `agent:review` / `ai_developed`, then adds `agent:dev` — so manually-dispatched dev legs (`gh workflow run … -f leg=dev`) show up on the board's Development lane, not just SM-armed ones. GitHub-tracker deployments only; non-fatal.
- New `pr_validation` lane between **PR created** and **Review**: open PRs with a dispatched validation run still in flight on the head (`queued`/`in_progress`/`waiting`/`pending`, no machine labels yet) render there instead of jumping straight to review.

### Key decisions
- Label assertion reuses smAgent's proven call shape (`workspace`/`repository`/`number`, singular `label` on removal — the gh-683 bug-D fix) and the trailing-number key parse; provider gated via `common/trackers.js` so Jira/ADO tickets are untouched.
- Lane rule lives in `factoryState.laneOf`: machine labels win first, then in-flight head verdict, then `pr_created` — `ACTIVE_RUN_STATES` mirrors `headVerdict`'s active filter.
- `pr_validation` has no `LANE_ENTERED_AT` stamp (derived state, not a label) — the board ages those cards from their newest `card.history` entry, same fallback as backlog columns.
- Lane order is additive in schema 2: `LANE_ORDER`, board `config.js`, and `laneSummary` (counts as in-flight) updated; schema-1 snapshots still render.

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_factoryState.json        # 59 passed
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_preCliDevelopmentSetup.json  # 16 passed
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_workingDir.json          # 16 passed

```

# gh-716: factory dashboard: dev leg must assert agent:dev itself + missing validation lane

## Description

Two gaps from the live dashboard review (2026-10-04):

1. **Development lane misses manually-dispatched dev legs.** Lane rule: issue has agent:dev AND NOT ai_developed. But agent:dev is only set by the SM when IT arms the leg — a manual dispatch (`gh workflow run ai-teammate.yml -f issue=N -f leg=dev`) bypasses labeling and the card vanishes from the board (live case: fa gh-1164, dev leg running 40+ min, Development column empty). Fix: the dev leg's setup (preCliDevelopmentSetup) asserts the transition itself — add agent:dev, clear stale agent:review/ai_developed — so any dispatch path shows correctly.

2. **No validation lane between PR Created and Review.** The real pipeline runs CI validation on the fresh PR head before/while review proceeds; the board jumps pr_created → review with no visible validation state. Add the lane (validation in-flight on the PR head) so a card's true position is visible.

Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 721
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/721
- **Title**: gh-716 factory dashboard: dev leg must assert agent:dev itself + missing validation lane
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-716` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 14
- **Additions**: +382
- **Deletions**: -17
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T20:43:45Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T20:43:45Z

## PR Description

### What changed
- `preCliDevelopmentSetup` now asserts the dev-leg transition itself: clears stale `agent:review` / `ai_developed`, then adds `agent:dev` — so manually-dispatched dev legs (`gh workflow run … -f leg=dev`) show up on the board's Development lane, not just SM-armed ones. GitHub-tracker deployments only; non-fatal.
- New `pr_validation` lane between **PR created** and **Review**: open PRs with a dispatched validation run still in flight on the head (`queued`/`in_progress`/`waiting`/`pending`, no machine labels yet) render there instead of jumping straight to review.

### Key decisions
- Label assertion reuses smAgent's proven call shape (`workspace`/`repository`/`number`, singular `label` on removal — the gh-683 bug-D fix) and the trailing-number key parse; provider gated via `common/trackers.js` so Jira/ADO tickets are untouched.
- Lane rule lives in `factoryState.laneOf`: machine labels win first, then in-flight head verdict, then `pr_created` — `ACTIVE_RUN_STATES` mirrors `headVerdict`'s active filter.
- `pr_validation` has no `LANE_ENTERED_AT` stamp (derived state, not a label) — the board ages those cards from their newest `card.history` entry, same fallback as backlog columns.
- Lane order is additive in schema 2: `LANE_ORDER`, board `config.js`, and `laneSummary` (counts as in-flight) updated; schema-1 snapshots still render.

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_factoryState.json        # 59 passed
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_preCliDevelopmentSetup.json  # 16 passed
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_workingDir.json          # 16 passed
bash site/factory/visual-check/capture.sh              # regenerated fixtures incl. PR validation lane
```

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  subgraph setup [preCliDevelopmentSetup — any dispatch path]
    D1[dev leg starts] --> D2[clear agent:review + ai_developed]
    D2 --> D3[add agent:dev]
    D3 --> D4[Development lane visible]
  end
  subgraph board [factoryState lanes]
    B1[pr_created] -->|head validation run in flight| B2[pr_validation]
    B2 --> B3[review · ai_pr_reviewed]
    B3 --> B4[approved_queue] --> B5[validating · mutex] --> B6[merged_recent]
  end
```

</details>

# gh-716: factory dashboard: dev leg must assert agent:dev itself + missing validation lane

## Description

Two gaps from the live dashboard review (2026-10-04):

1. **Development lane misses manually-dispatched dev legs.** Lane rule: issue has agent:dev AND NOT ai_developed. But agent:dev is only set by the SM when IT arms the leg — a manual dispatch (`gh workflow run ai-teammate.yml -f issue=N -f leg=dev`) bypasses labeling and the card vanishes from the board (live case: fa gh-1164, dev leg running 40+ min, Development column empty). Fix: the dev leg's setup (preCliDevelopmentSetup) asserts the transition itself — add agent:dev, clear stale agent:review/ai_developed — so any dispatch path shows correctly.

2. **No validation lane between PR Created and Review.** The real pipeline runs CI validation on the fresh PR head before/while review proceeds; the board jumps pr_created → review with no visible validation state. Add the lane (validation in-flight on the PR head) so a card's true position is visible.

## PR Description

### What changed
- `preCliDevelopmentSetup` now asserts the dev-leg transition itself: clears stale `agent:review` / `ai_developed`, then adds `agent:dev` — so manually-dispatched dev legs (`gh workflow run … -f leg=dev`) show up on the board's Development lane, not just SM-armed ones. GitHub-tracker deployments only; non-fatal.
- New `pr_validation` lane between **PR created** and **Review**: open PRs with a dispatched validation run still in flight on the head (`queued`/`in_progress`/`waiting`/`pending`, no machine labels yet) render there instead of jumping straight to review.

### Key decisions
- Label assertion reuses smAgent's proven call shape (`workspace`/`repository`/`number`, singular `label` on removal — the gh-683 bug-D fix) and the trailing-number key parse; provider gated via `common/trackers.js` so Jira/ADO tickets are untouched.
- Lane rule lives in `factoryState.laneOf`: machine labels win first, then in-flight head verdict, then `pr_created` — `ACTIVE_RUN_STATES` mirrors `headVerdict`'s active filter.
- `pr_validation` has no `LANE_ENTERED_AT` stamp (derived state, not a label) — the board ages those cards from their newest `card.history` entry, same fallback as backlog columns.
- Lane order is additive in schema 2: `LANE_ORDER`, board `config.js`, and `laneSummary` (counts as in-flight) updated; schema-1 snapshots still render.

```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_factoryState.json        # 59 passed

# gh-716: factory dashboard: dev leg must assert agent:dev itself + missing validation lane

## Description

Two gaps from the live dashboard review (2026-10-04):

1. **Development lane misses manually-dispatched dev legs.** Lane rule: issue has agent:dev AND NOT ai_developed. But agent:dev is only set by the SM when IT arms the leg — a manual dispatch (`gh workflow run ai-teammate.yml -f issue=N -f leg=dev`) bypasses labeling and the card vanishes from the board (live case: fa gh-1164, dev leg running 40+ min, Development column empty). Fix: the dev leg's setup (preCliDevelopmentSetup) asserts the transition itself — add agent:dev, clear stale agent:review/ai_developed — so any dispatch path shows correctly.

2. **No validation lane between PR Created and Review.** The real pipeline runs CI validation on the fresh PR head before/while review proceeds; the board jumps pr_created → review with no visible validation state. Add the lane (validation in-flight on the PR head) so a card's true position is visible.

### What changed
- `preCliDevelopmentSetup` now asserts the dev-leg transition itself: clears stale `agent:review` / `ai_developed`, then adds `agent:dev` — so manually-dispatched dev legs (`gh workflow run … -f leg=dev`) show up on the board's Development lane, not just SM-armed ones. - New `pr_validation` lane between **PR created** and **Review**: open PRs with a dispatched validation run still in flight on the head (`queued`/`in_progress`/`waiting`/`pending`, no machine labels yet) render there instead of jumping straight to review.

### Key decisions
- Label assertion reuses smAgent's proven call shape (`workspace`/`repository`/`number`, singular `label` on removal — the gh-683 bug-D fix) and the trailing-number key parse; provider gated via `common/trackers.js` so Jira/ADO tickets are untouched.

- `pr_validation` has no `LANE_ENTERED_AT` stamp (derived state, not a label) — the board ages those cards from their newest `card.history` entry, same fallback as backlog columns.
- Lane order is additive in schema 2: `LANE_ORDER`, board `config.js`, and `laneSummary` (counts as in-flight) updated; schema-1 snapshots still render.

# gh-716: factory dashboard: dev leg must assert agent:dev itself + missing validation lane

## Description

Two gaps from the live dashboard review (2026-10-04):

1. **Development lane misses manually-dispatched dev legs.** Lane rule: issue has agent:dev AND NOT ai_developed. But agent:dev is only set by the SM when IT arms the leg — a manual dispatch (`gh workflow run ai-teammate.yml -f issue=N -f leg=dev`) bypasses labeling and the card vanishes from the board (live case: fa gh-1164, dev leg running 40+ min, Development column empty). Fix: the dev leg's setup (preCliDevelopmentSetup) asserts the transition itself — add agent:dev, clear stale agent:review/ai_developed — so any dispatch path shows correctly.

2. **No validation lane between PR Created and Review.** The real pipeline runs CI validation on the fresh PR head before/while review proceeds; the board jumps pr_created → review with no visible validation state. Add the lane (validation in-flight on the PR head) so a card's true position is visible.

# gh-716: factory dashboard: dev leg must assert agent:dev itself + missing validation lane

## Description

Two gaps from the live dashboard review (2026-10-04):

1. **Development lane misses manually-dispatched dev legs.** Lane rule: issue has agent:dev AND NOT ai_developed. But agent:dev is only set by the SM when IT arms the leg — a manual dispatch (`gh workflow run ai-teammate.yml -f issue=N -f leg=dev`) bypasses labeling and the card vanishes from the board (live case: fa gh-1164, dev leg running 40+ min, Development column empty). Fix: the dev leg's setup (preCliDevelopmentSetup) asserts the transition itself — add agent:dev, clear stale agent:review/ai_developed — so any dispatch path shows correctly.

2. **No validation lane between PR Created and Review.** The real pipeline runs CI validation on the fresh PR head before/while review proceeds; the board jumps pr_created → review with no visible validation state. Add the lane (validation in-flight on the PR head) so a card's true position is visible.

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. ## PR Description

### What changed
- `preCliDevelopmentSetup` now asserts the dev-leg transition itself: clears stale `agent:review` / `ai_developed`, then adds `agent:dev` — so manually-dispatched dev legs (`gh workflow run … -f leg=dev`) show up on the board's Development lane, not just SM-armed ones. GitHub-tracker deployments only; non-fatal.

### Key decisions

## Description

1. **Development lane misses manually-dispatched dev legs.** Lane rule: issue has agent:dev AND NOT ai_developed. 2. **No validation lane between PR Created and Review.** The real pipeline runs CI validation on the fresh PR head before/while review proceeds; the board jumps pr_created → review with no visible validation state. Add the lane (validation in-flight on the PR head) so a card's true position is visible.

### Key decisions
- Label assertion reuses smAgent's proven call shape (`workspace`/`repository`/`number`, singular `label` on removal — the gh-683 bug-D fix) and the trailing-number key parse; provider gated via `common/trackers.js` so Jira/ADO tickets are untouched.

- `pr_validation` has no `LANE_ENTERED_AT` stamp (derived state, not a label) — the board ages those cards from their newest `card.history` entry, same fallback as backlog columns.
- Lane order is additive in schema 2: `LANE_ORDER`, board `config.js`, and `laneSummary` (counts as in-flight) updated; schema-1 snapshots still render.

# gh-716: factory dashboard: dev leg must assert agent:dev itself + missing validation lane

## Description

Two gaps from the live dashboard review (2026-10-04):

1. **Development lane misses manually-dispatched dev legs.** Lane rule: issue has agent:dev AND NOT ai_developed. But agent:dev is only set by the SM when IT arms the leg — a manual dispatch (`gh workflow run ai-teammate.yml -f issue=N -f leg=dev`) bypasses labeling and the card vanishes from the board (live case: fa gh-1164, dev leg running 40+ min, Development column empty). Fix: the dev leg's setup (preCliDevelopmentSetup) asserts the transition itself — add agent:dev, clear stale agent:review/ai_developed — so any dispatch path shows correctly.

2. **No validation lane between PR Created and Review.** The real pipeline runs CI validation on the fresh PR head before/while review proceeds; the board jumps pr_created → review with no visible validation state. Add the lane (validation in-flight on the PR head) so a card's true position is visible.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,

pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

# Pull Request Information

- **Title**: gh-716 factory dashboard: dev leg must assert agent:dev itself + missing validation lane
- **Author**: ai-teammate

- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 14
- **Additions**: +382
- **Deletions**: -17
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T20:43:45Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T20:43:45Z

## PR Description

### What changed
- `preCliDevelopmentSetup` now asserts the dev-leg transition itself: clears stale `agent:review` / `ai_developed`, then adds `agent:dev` — so manually-dispatched dev legs (`gh workflow run … -f leg=dev`) show up on the board's Development lane, not just SM-armed ones. GitHub-tracker deployments only; non-fatal.
- New `pr_validation` lane between **PR created** and **Review**: open PRs with a dispatched validation run still in flight on the head (`queued`/`in_progress`/`waiting`/`pending`, no machine labels yet) render there instead of jumping straight to review.

### Key decisions
- Label assertion reuses smAgent's proven call shape (`workspace`/`repository`/`number`, singular `label` on removal — the gh-683 bug-D fix) and the trailing-number key parse; provider gated via `common/trackers.js` so Jira/ADO tickets are untouched.
- Lane rule lives in `factoryState.laneOf`: machine labels win first, then in-flight head verdict, then `pr_created` — `ACTIVE_RUN_STATES` mirrors `headVerdict`'s active filter.
- `pr_validation` has no `LANE_ENTERED_AT` stamp (derived state, not a label) — the board ages those cards from their newest `card.history` entry, same fallback as backlog columns.
- Lane order is additive in schema 2: `LANE_ORDER`, board `config.js`, and `laneSummary` (counts as in-flight) updated; schema-1 snapshots still render.

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_factoryState.json        # 59 passed
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_preCliDevelopmentSetup.json  # 16 passed
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_workingDir.json          # 16 passed
bash site/factory/visual-check/capture.sh              # regenerated fixtures incl. PR validation lane
```

# gh-716: factory dashboard: dev leg must assert agent:dev itself + missing validation lane

## Description

Two gaps from the live dashboard review (2026-10-04):

1. **Development lane misses manually-dispatched dev legs.** Lane rule: issue has agent:dev AND NOT ai_developed. But agent:dev is only set by the SM when IT arms the leg — a manual dispatch (`gh workflow run ai-teammate.yml -f issue=N -f leg=dev`) bypasses labeling and the card vanishes from the board (live case: fa gh-1164, dev leg running 40+ min, Development column empty). Fix: the dev leg's setup (preCliDevelopmentSetup) asserts the transition itself — add agent:dev, clear stale agent:review/ai_developed — so any dispatch path shows correctly.

2. **No validation lane between PR Created and Review.** The real pipeline runs CI validation on the fresh PR head before/while review proceeds; the board jumps pr_created → review with no visible validation state. Add the lane (validation in-flight on the PR head) so a card's true position is visible.

- `preCliDevelopmentSetup` now asserts the dev-leg transition itself: clears stale `agent:review` / `ai_developed`, then adds `agent:dev` — so manually-dispatched dev legs (`gh workflow run … -f leg=dev`) show up on the board's Development lane, not just SM-armed ones. ### Key decisions
- Label assertion reuses smAgent's proven call shape (`workspace`/`repository`/`number`, singular `label` on removal — the gh-683 bug-D fix) and the trailing-number key parse; provider gated via `common/trackers.js` so Jira/ADO tickets are untouched.

- `pr_validation` has no `LANE_ENTERED_AT` stamp (derived state, not a label) — the board ages those cards from their newest `card.history` entry, same fallback as backlog columns.
- Lane order is additive in schema 2: `LANE_ORDER`, board `config.js`, and `laneSummary` (counts as in-flight) updated; schema-1 snapshots still render.

# gh-716: factory dashboard: dev leg must assert agent:dev itself + missing validation lane

## Description

Two gaps from the live dashboard review (2026-10-04):

1. **Development lane misses manually-dispatched dev legs.** Lane rule: issue has agent:dev AND NOT ai_developed. But agent:dev is only set by the SM when IT arms the leg — a manual dispatch (`gh workflow run ai-teammate.yml -f issue=N -f leg=dev`) bypasses labeling and the card vanishes from the board (live case: fa gh-1164, dev leg running 40+ min, Development column empty). Fix: the dev leg's setup (preCliDevelopmentSetup) asserts the transition itself — add agent:dev, clear stale agent:review/ai_developed — so any dispatch path shows correctly.

2. **No validation lane between PR Created and Review.** The real pipeline runs CI validation on the fresh PR head before/while review proceeds; the board jumps pr_created → review with no visible validation state. Add the lane (validation in-flight on the PR head) so a card's true position is visible.

- Lane order is additive in schema 2: `LANE_ORDER`, board `config.js`, and `laneSummary` (counts as in-flight) updated; schema-1 snapshots still render.

# gh-716: factory dashboard: dev leg must assert agent:dev itself + missing validation lane

## Description

Two gaps from the live dashboard review (2026-10-04):

1. **Development lane misses manually-dispatched dev legs.** Lane rule: issue has agent:dev AND NOT ai_developed. But agent:dev is only set by the SM when IT arms the leg — a manual dispatch (`gh workflow run ai-teammate.yml -f issue=N -f leg=dev`) bypasses labeling and the card vanishes from the board (live case: fa gh-1164, dev leg running 40+ min, Development column empty). Fix: the dev leg's setup (preCliDevelopmentSetup) asserts the transition itself — add agent:dev, clear stale agent:review/ai_developed — so any dispatch path shows correctly.

2. **No validation lane between PR Created and Review.** The real pipeline runs CI validation on the fresh PR head before/while review proceeds; the board jumps pr_created → review with no visible validation state. Add the lane (validation in-flight on the PR head) so a card's true position is visible.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

But agent:dev is only set by the SM when IT arms the leg — a manual dispatch (`gh workflow run ai-teammate.yml -f issue=N -f leg=dev`) bypasses labeling and the card vanishes from the board (live case: fa gh-1164, dev leg running 40+ min, Development column empty). Fix: the dev leg's setup (preCliDevelopmentSetup) asserts the transition itself — add agent:dev, clear stale agent:review/ai_developed — so any dispatch path shows correctly.\n\n2. **No validation lane between PR Created and Review.** The real pipeline runs CI validation on the fresh PR head before/while review proceeds; the board jumps pr_created → review with no visible validation state. Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,

pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. ## PR Description

### What changed
- `preCliDevelopmentSetup` now asserts the dev-leg transition itself: clears stale `agent:review` / `ai_developed`, then adds `agent:dev` — so manually-dispatched dev legs (`gh workflow run … -f leg=dev`) show up on the board's Development lane, not just SM-armed ones. GitHub-tracker deployments only; non-fatal.
- New `pr_validation` lane between **PR created** and **Review**: open PRs with a dispatched validation run still in flight on the head (`queued`/`in_progress`/`waiting`/`pending`, no machine labels yet) render there instead of jumping straight to review.

### Key decisions
- Label assertion reuses smAgent's proven call shape (`workspace`/`repository`/`number`, singular `label` on removal — the gh-683 bug-D fix) and the trailing-number key parse; provider gated via `common/trackers.js` so Jira/ADO tickets are untouched.
- Lane rule lives in `factoryState.laneOf`: machine labels win first, then in-flight head verdict, then `pr_created` — `ACTIVE_RUN_STATES` mirrors `headVerdict`'s active filter.
- `pr_validation` has no `LANE_ENTERED_AT` stamp (derived state, not a label) — the board ages those cards from their newest `card.history` entry, same fallback as backlog columns.
- Lane order is additive in schema 2: `LANE_ORDER`, board `config.js`, and `laneSummary` (counts as in-flight) updated; schema-1 snapshots still render.

```bash

# gh-716: factory dashboard: dev leg must assert agent:dev itself + missing validation lane

## Description

Two gaps from the live dashboard review (2026-10-04):

1. **Development lane misses manually-dispatched dev legs.** Lane rule: issue has agent:dev AND NOT ai_developed. But agent:dev is only set by the SM when IT arms the leg — a manual dispatch (`gh workflow run ai-teammate.yml -f issue=N -f leg=dev`) bypasses labeling and the card vanishes from the board (live case: fa gh-1164, dev leg running 40+ min, Development column empty). Fix: the dev leg's setup (preCliDevelopmentSetup) asserts the transition itself — add agent:dev, clear stale agent:review/ai_developed — so any dispatch path shows correctly.

2. **No validation lane between PR Created and Review.** The real pipeline runs CI validation on the fresh PR head before/while review proceeds; the board jumps pr_created → review with no visible validation state. Add the lane (validation in-flight on the PR head) so a card's true position is visible.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## PR Description

### What changed
- `preCliDevelopmentSetup` now asserts the dev-leg transition itself: clears stale `agent:review` / `ai_developed`, then adds `agent:dev` — so manually-dispatched dev legs (`gh workflow run … -f leg=dev`) show up on the board's Development lane, not just SM-armed ones. GitHub-tracker deployments only; non-fatal.
- New `pr_validation` lane between **PR created** and **Review**: open PRs with a dispatched validation run still in flight on the head (`queued`/`in_progress`/`waiting`/`pending`, no machine labels yet) render there instead of jumping straight to review.

### Key decisions
- Label assertion reuses smAgent's proven call shape (`workspace`/`repository`/`number`, singular `label` on removal — the gh-683 bug-D fix) and the trailing-number key parse; provider gated via `common/trackers.js` so Jira/ADO tickets are untouched.
- Lane rule lives in `factoryState.laneOf`: machine labels win first, then in-flight head verdict, then `pr_created` — `ACTIVE_RUN_STATES` mirrors `headVerdict`'s active filter.
- `pr_validation` has no `LANE_ENTERED_AT` stamp (derived state, not a label) — the board ages those cards from their newest `card.history` entry, same fallback as backlog columns.
- Lane order is additive in schema 2: `LANE_ORDER`, board `config.js`, and `laneSummary` (counts as in-flight) updated; schema-1 snapshots still render.

# gh-716: factory dashboard: dev leg must assert agent:dev itself + missing validation lane

## Description

Two gaps from the live dashboard review (2026-10-04):

1. **Development lane misses manually-dispatched dev legs.** Lane rule: issue has agent:dev AND NOT ai_developed. But agent:dev is only set by the SM when IT arms the leg — a manual dispatch (`gh workflow run ai-teammate.yml -f issue=N -f leg=dev`) bypasses labeling and the card vanishes from the board (live case: fa gh-1164, dev leg running 40+ min, Development column empty). Fix: the dev leg's setup (preCliDevelopmentSetup) asserts the transition itself — add agent:dev, clear stale agent:review/ai_developed — so any dispatch path shows correctly.

2. **No validation lane between PR Created and Review.** The real pipeline runs CI validation on the fresh PR head before/while review proceeds; the board jumps pr_created → review with no visible validation state. Add the lane (validation in-flight on the PR head) so a card's true position is visible.

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## PR Description

### What changed
- `preCliDevelopmentSetup` now asserts the dev-leg transition itself: clears stale `agent:review` / `ai_developed`, then adds `agent:dev` — so manually-dispatched dev legs (`gh workflow run … -f leg=dev`) show up on the board's Development lane, not just SM-armed ones. GitHub-tracker deployments only; non-fatal.
- New `pr_validation` lane between **PR created** and **Review**: open PRs with a dispatched validation run still in flight on the head (`queued`/`in_progress`/`waiting`/`pending`, no machine labels yet) render there instead of jumping straight to review.

### Key decisions
- Label assertion reuses smAgent's proven call shape (`workspace`/`repository`/`number`, singular `label` on removal — the gh-683 bug-D fix) and the trailing-number key parse; provider gated via `common/trackers.js` so Jira/ADO tickets are untouched.
- Lane rule lives in `factoryState.laneOf`: machine labels win first, then in-flight head verdict, then `pr_created` — `ACTIVE_RUN_STATES` mirrors `headVerdict`'s active filter.
- `pr_validation` has no `LANE_ENTERED_AT` stamp (derived state, not a label) — the board ages those cards from their newest `card.history` entry, same fallback as backlog columns.
- Lane order is additive in schema 2: `LANE_ORDER`, board `config.js`, and `laneSummary` (counts as in-flight) updated; schema-1 snapshots still render.

# gh-716: factory dashboard: dev leg must assert agent:dev itself + missing validation lane

## Description

Two gaps from the live dashboard review (2026-10-04):

1. **Development lane misses manually-dispatched dev legs.** Lane rule: issue has agent:dev AND NOT ai_developed. But agent:dev is only set by the SM when IT arms the leg — a manual dispatch (`gh workflow run ai-teammate.yml -f issue=N -f leg=dev`) bypasses labeling and the card vanishes from the board (live case: fa gh-1164, dev leg running 40+ min, Development column empty). Fix: the dev leg's setup (preCliDevelopmentSetup) asserts the transition itself — add agent:dev, clear stale agent:review/ai_developed — so any dispatch path shows correctly.

2. **No validation lane between PR Created and Review.** The real pipeline runs CI validation on the fresh PR head before/while review proceeds; the board jumps pr_created → review with no visible validation state. Add the lane (validation in-flight on the PR head) so a card's true position is visible.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

### Key decisions
- Label assertion reuses smAgent's proven call shape (`workspace`/`repository`/`number`, singular `label` on removal — the gh-683 bug-D fix) and the trailing-number key parse; provider gated via `common/trackers.js` so Jira/ADO tickets are untouched.

- `pr_validation` has no `LANE_ENTERED_AT` stamp (derived state, not a label) — the board ages those cards from their newest `card.history` entry, same fallback as backlog columns.
- Lane order is additive in schema 2: `LANE_ORDER`, board `config.js`, and `laneSummary` (counts as in-flight) updated; schema-1 snapshots still render.

# gh-716: factory dashboard: dev leg must assert agent:dev itself + missing validation lane

## Description

Two gaps from the live dashboard review (2026-10-04):

1. **Development lane misses manually-dispatched dev legs.** Lane rule: issue has agent:dev AND NOT ai_developed. But agent:dev is only set by the SM when IT arms the leg — a manual dispatch (`gh workflow run ai-teammate.yml -f issue=N -f leg=dev`) bypasses labeling and the card vanishes from the board (live case: fa gh-1164, dev leg running 40+ min, Development column empty). Fix: the dev leg's setup (preCliDevelopmentSetup) asserts the transition itself — add agent:dev, clear stale agent:review/ai_developed — so any dispatch path shows correctly.

2. **No validation lane between PR Created and Review.** The real pipeline runs CI validation on the fresh PR head before/while review proceeds; the board jumps pr_created → review with no visible validation state. Add the lane (validation in-flight on the PR head) so a card's true position is visible.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

### Key decisions
- Label assertion reuses smAgent's proven call shape (`workspace`/`repository`/`number`, singular `label` on removal — the gh-683 bug-D fix) and the trailing-number key parse; provider gated via `common/trackers.js` so Jira/ADO tickets are untouched.

- Lane order is additive in schema 2: `LANE_ORDER`, board `config.js`, and `laneSummary` (counts as in-flight) updated; schema-1 snapshots still render.

# gh-716: factory dashboard: dev leg must assert agent:dev itself + missing validation lane

## Description

Two gaps from the live dashboard review (2026-10-04):

1. **Development lane misses manually-dispatched dev legs.** Lane rule: issue has agent:dev AND NOT ai_developed. But agent:dev is only set by the SM when IT arms the leg — a manual dispatch (`gh workflow run ai-teammate.yml -f issue=N -f leg=dev`) bypasses labeling and the card vanishes from the board (live case: fa gh-1164, dev leg running 40+ min, Development column empty). Fix: the dev leg's setup (preCliDevelopmentSetup) asserts the transition itself — add agent:dev, clear stale agent:review/ai_developed — so any dispatch path shows correctly.

2. **No validation lane between PR Created and Review.** The real pipeline runs CI validation on the fresh PR head before/while review proceeds; the board jumps pr_created → review with no visible validation state. Add the lane (validation in-flight on the PR head) so a card's true position is visible.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

blocks.text:
Wiring is complete. Now check the CI status — no ci_failures.md input, so no CI failures to report. PR is from ai-teammate; machine-merge will validate.

Final sweep of remaining nits for the exhaustive pass:

1. **`run_workingDir.json` missing trailing newline** — trivial (many JSON files in repo; check convention). Check other run_*.json files for trailing newline.

2. **Indentation inconsistency in test_workingDir.js** — the two later mock blocks got `'./common/trackers.js': trackersModuleReal` at wrong indent (12 spaces vs 16) and a dangling `,` on its own line pattern. Minor style.

3. **fixture.json pr_validation PR number 872** — bigger than others; check fixture's other PR numbers to make sure it doesn't break any drawer/timeline tests. Not a functional concern.

4. **Duplication of the mock loader** in test_preCliDevelopmentSetup.js: `loadPreCliDevelopmentSetupWithExtras` duplicates the require map from `loadPreCliDevelopmentSetup` — the pre-existing helper was not reused; the new suite defines a parallel full-stub loader. SUGGESTION: could refactor to share, but acceptable given different stub needs (they pass a config loader stub vs NOOPs).

Actually wait — the existing `loadPreCliDevelopmentSetup(configLoaderStub, mocks)` already takes a configLoaderStub and mocks. The new suite could have used it with the extras... but it needed `./config.js` as NOOP_CONFIG_JS and setupCommands stubs which the existing helper already supplies. Actually looking at existing helper: it uses makeRequire with './configLoader.js': configLoaderStub, plus NOOP modules, then `mocks || {}`. The new `loadPreCliDevelopmentSetupWithExtras` builds essentially the same require map inline (duplicating ~12 lines). The only difference: github behavior mocks. The existing helper accepts `mocks` — the new suite could have called `loadPreCliDevelopmentSetup(makeActionConfigLoaderStub(config), {cli_execute_command..., jira_move_to_status..., github_add_labels..., github_remove_label...})`. That's exactly the same thing without duplicating the require map. So ~15 lines of duplication introduced. SUGGESTION-level.

Wait — actually check: existing helper's makeRequire includes './common/trackers.js': trackersModuleReal now. Yes, it was updated. So the new loader is pure duplication. SUGGESTION.

5. **`assertDevLegTransition` silently swallows ALL removal errors** — a transient GitHub failure removing 'ai_developed' would leave ai_developed on, and the Development lane rule (agent:dev AND NOT ai_developed) would keep the card hidden — the exact bug this PR fixes remains possible on a transient failure, silently. But it's non-fatal by design and logged only for outer errors; removal errors are swallowed entirely with no log. SUGGESTION: log a warning on unexpected removal errors. Minor.

6. **`console.log('Cleared stale ' + label ...)`** — logs "Cleared stale" even though in the failure case nothing was cleared... no, it only logs when no throw. But gh CLI remove-label might succeed silently even if label absent (exit 0 "Label not found"?). Depends on the bridge; harmless.

7. **laneOf: `checks.verdict` of 'cancelled'?** — headVerdict never returns 'cancelled' as state (conclusion 'cancelled' excluded from terminal, and status filter only has the four active states). Consistent.

8. **app.js laneSummary order of conditions**: `hasBlocked(c)` wins; then mergedAt; then lane inflight for pr_validation. A blocked card in pr_validation counts blocked. Good.

9. **Schema-1 board render**: `laneHtml` is driven by `CFG.lanes` — schema 1 snapshots render the new empty 'PR validation' column. PR description says "schema-1 snapshots still render" — meaning they don't break, but they'll show an empty extra column. Acceptable/intended.

10. **`pr_validation` in the drawer's laneTitle map** (line ~238 `laneTitle`)? Check: `function laneTitle(key)` at line 238 maps lane keys to titles from CFG.lanes — config-driven, so 'PR validation' resolves. Good.

11. **counts in fixture**: `counts` updated to include pr_validation. Good.

12. **Em-dash in console.log strings** — fine.

13. One more potential issue: **ticket key parse `/(\d+)$/`** — for key like 'gh-716' fine. But a Jira key 'PROJ-10' would parse to 10 — gated behind provider()==='github' so only gh keys reach it. But what about a github-tracked key that's not gh-N? e.g. plain '716' or 'GH-716' — handled. OK.

14. **`params.number = parseInt(m[1],10)`** matches smAgent.

15. Is there a check that `assertDevLegTransition` placement happens AFTER the ticket exists? It's step 1.5, uses only ticketKey. Fine.

16. **GraalJS: `Object.assign`** — already used elsewhere in the file (line 451 context shows Object.assign used). Fine.

17. Check `test_factoryState.js` — 'waiting' in ACTIVE_RUN_STATES test missing 'pending'? Test covers in_progress, queued, waiting — 'pending' not tested. Trivial coverage nit — could add. SUGGESTION.

18. **`input/TICKET/pr_files.txt`** — not present; we have the diff stat from git.

19. Double-check `fixture.json` head sha and history at consistency for the visual check: pr_validation card history second entry at "2026-10-03T11:52:00Z" equals checks.at. Good.

20. **The fixture's `pr` number 872 > 860** in review — but review lane isn't FIFO-sorted with pr_validation; different lanes, fine.

Verdict: No BLOCKING. A few SUGGESTIONs and maybe one IMPORTANT? Let me evaluate severity:

- Duplicated loader in test file: SUGGESTION.
- Silent swallow of removal errors with no logging: SUGGESTION (non-fatal by design; debuggability nit).
- 'pending' state untested in unit test: SUGGESTION.
- run_workingDir.json no trailing newline: SUGGESTION.
- Indentation in test_workingDir.js: SUGGESTION.

Is there anything IMPORTANT? Let me think about correctness once more...

**Potential real correctness concern**: In `laneOf`, a PR with `ai_pr_reviewed` label AND an active head validation run shows in 'review'. But in the rework flow, after review the machine dispatches a *rework* dev leg whose runs are workflow_dispatch on a new head sha — the PR head changes when new commits are pushed. headVerdict filters by head_sha, so old runs on previous heads don't count. Good.

**Another**: when the machine dispatches the *validation* run for a fresh PR (the real pipeline: "CI validation on the fresh PR head before/while review"), is that run a `workflow_dispatch`? If the factory's validation is a `pull_request`-triggered CI workflow, headVerdict (workflow_dispatch-only) would never see it, and pr_validation would stay empty. But the machine's own validation legs (pr_validation job like this one) are dispatched via workflow_dispatch — "open PRs with a dispatched validation run still in flight on the head". The gh-716 ticket itself says "a dispatched validation run". Consistent with scope. Not a blocker; the limitation is documented in the comment? The comment says "a dispatched run on the head". OK.

**One more check — `ACTIVE_RUN_STATES` mirrors headVerdict**: headVerdict's active filter is exactly those 4 states. Verified identical. 

**Check pr.checks null case**: `laneOf({labels: [], checks: null})` → pr_created. Tested.

**Check issue-side**: laneOf only called for PR cards. OK.

**Backward compat of module.exports addition**: additive. OK.

**One thing**: `js/unit-tests/run_workingDir.json` uses 1-space indentation while other run_*.json files? Check convention.
Final checks on test conventions and remaining details:

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. ## PR Description

### What changed
- `preCliDevelopmentSetup` now asserts the dev-leg transition itself: clears stale `agent:review` / `ai_developed`, then adds `agent:dev` — so manually-dispatched dev legs (`gh workflow run … -f leg=dev`) show up on the board's Development lane, not just SM-armed ones. GitHub-tracker deployments only; non-fatal.
- New `pr_validation` lane between **PR created** and **Review**: open PRs with a dispatched validation run still in flight on the head (`queued`/`in_progress`/`waiting`/`pending`, no machine labels yet) render there instead of jumping straight to review.

### Key decisions
- Label assertion reuses smAgent's proven call shape (`workspace`/`repository`/`number`, singular `label` on removal — the gh-683 bug-D fix) and the trailing-number key parse; provider gated via `common/trackers.js` so Jira/ADO tickets are untouched.
- Lane rule lives in `factoryState.laneOf`: machine labels win first, then in-flight head verdict, then `pr_created` — `ACTIVE_RUN_STATES` mirrors `headVerdict`'s active filter.
- `pr_validation` has no `LANE_ENTERED_AT` stamp (derived state, not a label) — the board ages those cards from their newest `card.history` entry, same fallback as backlog columns.
- Lane order is additive in schema 2: `LANE_ORDER`, board `config.js`, and `laneSummary` (counts as in-flight) updated; schema-1 snapshots still render.

# gh-716: factory dashboard: dev leg must assert agent:dev itself + missing validation lane

## Description

Two gaps from the live dashboard review (2026-10-04):

1. **Development lane misses manually-dispatched dev legs.** Lane rule: issue has agent:dev AND NOT ai_developed. But agent:dev is only set by the SM when IT arms the leg — a manual dispatch (`gh workflow run ai-teammate.yml -f issue=N -f leg=dev`) bypasses labeling and the card vanishes from the board (live case: fa gh-1164, dev leg running 40+ min, Development column empty). Fix: the dev leg's setup (preCliDevelopmentSetup) asserts the transition itself — add agent:dev, clear stale agent:review/ai_developed — so any dispatch path shows correctly.

2. **No validation lane between PR Created and Review.** The real pipeline runs CI validation on the fresh PR head before/while review proceeds; the board jumps pr_created → review with no visible validation state. Add the lane (validation in-flight on the PR head) so a card's true position is visible.
